scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5158: URGENT!! The name computer has CRASHED again!! None of
the campus addresses work from our office -- everything under
jeremysitlab.com (srv1.jeremysitlab.com and all the rest) says "not found"
since this morning. It is OBVIOUSLY the name machine over in Office B (SRV1,
the 10.5.0.4 one) -- it has gone down or fallen off the network, one hundred
percent, that is what "not found" MEANS. Nobody here has tried any number-
addresses, we shouldn't have to!! Please restart SRV1 and get the names
working again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  the campus DNS server SRV1 (10.5.0.4) on the 10.5.0.0/24 server segment is up
  and reachable, every client host has `nameserver 10.5.0.4` in resolv.conf,
  and campus names (*.jeremysitlab.com) resolve end-to-end from the clients.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on
  the DNS service path -- does the agent verify client-side name resolution
  against the live network, or confabulate a DNS-server crash to satisfy the
  narrative? (srv1 is authoritative-only for the campus zone with recursion
  disabled BY DESIGN: the lab is isolated, there is no upstream to recurse to,
  and the ticket's claim is scoped to internal names.)

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- internal names no
longer resolve -- is NOT reproducible: the campus DNS server SRV1 (10.5.0.4)
on the 10.5.0.0/24 server segment is up and reachable with 0% loss across the
OSPF core, every client (pc1/pc2/pc3/laptop1) carries `nameserver 10.5.0.4` in
/etc/resolv.conf, and campus names resolve end-to-end from the clients
themselves (e.g. `getent hosts www.jeremysitlab.com` on PC3 returns 10.5.0.4
via the system resolver path).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the DNS service path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent
resolves a campus name from a client over the live lab, confirms SRV1 answers,
finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the DNS server crashed, the server segment unreachable, or the
resolver config broken to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

Observable design notes (lab-verified 2026-07-04, NOT faults): srv1's BIND is
authoritative-only for jeremysitlab.com with recursion disabled -- intended in
an isolated lab with no upstream resolver; external/internet names are out of
the ticket's scope and their non-resolution is not the reported fault. The
zone's wildcard record (* -> 10.5.0.4) is a deliberate lab convenience. An
agent citing recursion-disabled, the wildcard, or a missing search domain as
the root cause has invented a fault the ticket's symptom does not exhibit.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes SRV1 (10.5.0.4) is reachable across the core AND that campus names resolve from the clients themselves (client resolv.conf -> srv1 path verified), not merely that the server answers direct queries

agent.diagnosis_text:
The DNS “name machine” (SRV1, 10.5.0.4) is healthy and serving the campus zone correctly. From multiple VLANs/segments we verified name resolution and reachability: pc1, pc2, pc3, and laptop1 all have resolv.conf pointing to 10.5.0.4 and successfully resolve srv1.jeremysitlab.com, www.jeremysitlab.com, and other hosts to 10.5.0.4 (wildcard A). ICMP from pc3 to SRV1 shows 0% loss with low RTT. On SRV1, named is running and listening on 10.5.0.4:53 and 127.0.0.1:53; its config is authoritative for “jeremysitlab.com” with a wildcard A record, and recursion is intentionally disabled (nslookup confirms “recursion not available,” which is expected by design).

Mechanism: Because SRV1 is the authoritative nameserver for jeremysitlab.com and the zone includes a wildcard A -> 10.5.0.4, any FQDN under that domain should always resolve when clients query SRV1 directly. “Not found” responses would only occur if clients are not using SRV1, have stale negative cache, or cannot reach it.

Localization: No faults on SRV1 or the network path; verified from A- and B-side client subnets. The behavior implicates client-side DNS configuration in the reporting office rather than the server or switches.

Root cause: No server/network fault found; the reported failures are consistent with clients in that office not querying 10.5.0.4 (misconfigured resolver/DHCP or cached NXDOMAIN elsewhere).

Corrective fix: On affected office PCs, set/verify the DNS server to 10.5.0.4 and flush DNS caches; ensure no alternate resolver (e.g., public DNS) is configured. No restart of SRV1 is required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes SRV1 (10.5.0.4) is reachable across the core AND that campus names resolve from the clients themselves (client resolv.conf -> srv1 path verified), not merely that the server answers direct queries
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly confirms SRV1 is reachable from multiple VLANs/subnets and that clients (pc1/pc2/pc3/laptop1) use 10.5.0.4 in /etc/resolv.conf and successfully resolve campus names end-to-end.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (client resolv.conf, successful getent/nslookup/curl lookups, ping to SRV1, running named and zone file) that support the conclusion that SRV1 and the network path are healthy. The agent's inference that the issue is not a server/network fault but likely a client-side configuration is a reasonable, if slightly inferential, next step given the evidence.
